# FLX-3505: a sink could not finish writing a stream

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

The destination refused a write part-way: a disk filled up, a permission was missing, a file could not be renamed into place, an object store could not be set up or refused an upload, or a read-back check found data that does not digest to the stream's outputDigest. A file sink writing to a local directory stages every file under a hidden name and renames it into place only when the whole stream is written, and it removes what it staged when it fails, so no partial stream is left for a reader to mistake for a whole one. On an object store, data objects that were uploaded before the failure can stay behind without the manifest that completes them; a stream is whole only when its manifest object is there. An object store failure that comes of the credentials or the endpoint ends with the settings to check: the AWS_* variables and AWS_ALLOW_HTTP for s3://, GOOGLE_* for gs://, AZURE_* for az:// and abfs://. The message names variables, never their values. An object store target with no credential in the environment is refused before the run, with nothing contacted, because the store would otherwise ask the cloud's instance metadata service (169.254.169.254 and its siblings) for one; to use the credentials of the machine or workload the run is on (an instance role, a pod or managed identity), pass --sink-opt instance-identity=true. Whatever the target, the run directory and its outputDigest are unaffected and the run is kept: after the cause is fixed, publish it again with fluxsim apply BUNDLE --run-id RUN_ID --sink TARGET (the command prints it, with --state-dir when one was given), which writes the same files under the same names.

## Look it up offline

```console
$ fluxsim explain FLX-3505
```
